rows.text: August 11, 2009
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the Base Rate at its current level (2.00%) for the intermeeting period.

Monetary Policy Decision
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the Base Rate at its current level (2.00%) for the intermeeting period.
Domestic economic activity is sustaining its improved movements thanks to the proactive fiscal and monetary policy strive and the upturn of the economic situation in emerging markets.
The slump in domestic demand and exports has moderated further.
(The following is an unofficial English translation of the Monetary Policy Committee statement.)
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the Base Rate at its current level (2.00%) for the intermeeting period.
There still remains uncertainty as to the economic growth path due to the likelihood of delay in the recovery of the major advanced economies.
Consumer price inflation has continued to decelerate thanks to the easing of demand-pull pressures and the won's appreciation.
Domestic economic activity is sustaining its improved movements thanks to the proactive fiscal and monetary policy strive and the upturn of the economic situation in emerging markets.
The slump in domestic demand and exports has moderated further.
The upward trend of real estate prices has been maintained.
There still remains uncertainty as to the economic growth path due to the likelihood of delay in the recovery of the major advanced economies.
Market interest rates and stock prices have risen.
Mortgage loans continued to expand markedly.
Consumer price inflation has continued to decelerate thanks to the easing of demand-pull pressures and the won's appreciation.
The upward trend of real estate prices has been maintained.
Meanwhile, concerns about credit risk and the shortermism of market funds have not been resolved.

Looking ahead, the Committee will maintain accommodative policy stance for the time being and do what is needed to bring about the continuation of the recent improving pattern of economic movements and financial market stabilization.
